_doc: Reviewed table for tools/build-claim-placement.mjs. `approach`, `stops` and `departures` name the ledger claims that become an approach road (AP), a stop (PO) or a departure (DP); each row carries the phrase that makes it literal (phrase_in: the claim's verified quote, its printed place words, its printed road words, or the cited OR record as confirmed by tools/verify_claim_phrases.py), and why. `approach_exclude`, `stops_exclude` and `departures_exclude` give, for every claim that passes the mechanical tests and is NOT used, the reason. A claim that passes the tests and is in none of the six lists stops the build. Read by hand; the builder re-checks everything it can.

approach.phrase: Emmitsburg pike
approach.identification: printed as the Emmitsburg pike; the gazetteer road is Emmitsburg Road (the ledger references GZ-041)
approach.why: The 2nd Wisconsin approached Gettysburg from the Emmitsburg pike on the morning of 1 July; the same road as AP-01 (the PDF ledger row of I Corps).

approach.phrase: the road running from Emmitsburg to Gettysburg
approach.identification: printed as the road running from Emmitsburg to Gettysburg; the ledger references GZ-041, Emmitsburg Road
approach.why: The 7th Wisconsin left its camp on that road about 5 miles from Gettysburg early on 1 July and marched in column behind the 2nd.

approach.phrase: Emmitsburg road
approach.why: Schurz's account: the First Division under Barlow arrived by the Emmitsburg road proper and advanced through the town (1 July).

approach.phrase: Gettysburg and Hanover road
approach.identification: printed as the Gettysburg and Hanover road; the gazetteer road is Hanover Road (the ledger references GZ-043)
approach.why: The Second Division of V Corps marched forward on the night of 1-2 July on the Gettysburg and Hanover road.

approach.phrase: broad and excellent pike leading direct to Gettysburg
approach.identification: the pike is named the Baltimore and Gettysburg pike in claim POS-C-0214 of the same report and referenced as GZ-039 (Baltimore Pike) in POS-C-0212; the identification is the ledger's, not a second source
approach.why: VI Corps marched the last stretch on the pike leading direct to Gettysburg (Wright's report).

approach.phrase: pike leading from Gettysburg to Hanover
approach.identification: printed as the pike leading from Gettysburg to Hanover; the gazetteer road is Hanover Road (the ledger references GZ-043). The place is stated as about 2 miles from Gettysburg, which lies beyond the east edge of the loaded ground
approach.why: J. I. Gregg's brigade arrived and took position on the pike leading from Gettysburg to Hanover, about 2 miles from Gettysburg, about 11 a. m. on 2 July.

approach.phrase: down the turnpike road leading to Gettysburg
approach.identification: a turnpike leading to Gettysburg from near Cashtown: the Chambersburg Pike (the ledger references GZ-075 Cashtown and prints Cashtown-Gettysburg turnpike); the name Chambersburg Pike is the gazetteer's
approach.why: Archer's brigade left camp near Cashtown early on 1 July and marched down the turnpike road leading to Gettysburg (report of Lt. Col. Shepard).

approach.phrase: by a turninke road leading to Gettysburg
approach.identification: a turnpike road leading to Gettysburg from camp near Cashtown (OCR "turninke"): the Chambersburg Pike
approach.why: Davis's brigade moved in rear of Archer's from camp on the heights near Cashtown by a turnpike road leading to Gettysburg.

approach.phrase: road leading from Chambersburg to Gettysburg
approach.identification: the turnpike road leading from Chambersburg to Gettysburg, half way between Cashtown and Gettysburg: the Chambersburg Pike
approach.why: Pettigrew's brigade picketed that turnpike on the night of 30 June and moved down the pike toward Gettysburg early on 1 July (report of Maj. Jones).

approach.phrase: along the turn]uke through Cashtown
approach.identification: the turnpike through Cashtown toward Gettysburg (OCR "turn]uke"): the Chambersburg Pike
approach.why: Pender's division moved at an hour damaged in the OCR on the morning of 1 July along the turnpike through Cashtown in the direction of Gettysburg, in rear of Heth's division; McGowan's brigade report prints the turnpike leading to Gettysburg.

approach.phrase: Chambersburg and Gettysburg turnpike
approach.why: Wilcox's brigade moved forward on the Chambersburg and Gettysburg turnpike on the morning of 1 July.

approach.phrase: marching on the Cashtown road
approach.identification: printed as the Cashtown road, the road from Cashtown to Gettysburg: the gazetteer's Chambersburg Pike (the ledger references GZ-040)
approach.why: Nicholls's brigade, in front of Johnson's division, was marching on the Cashtown road toward Gettysburg about 7 o'clock on 1 July when it was ordered east of the town.

approach.phrase: moving along the Chambersburg road
approach.identification: printed as the Chambersburg road: the gazetteer's Chambersburg Pike (alias Chambersburg Road)
approach.why: Latimer moved the battalion from its camp near Chambersburg on 1 July along the Chambersburg road and appeared in front of Gettysburg just before dark.

approach.phrase: on the Emmitsburg road
approach.why: Hancock: the head of the Third Corps appeared in sight on the Emmitsburg road shortly after Slocum arrived (between 5 and 6 o'clock on 1 July).

approach.phrase: by way of the Emmitsburg road
approach.why: The 99th Pennsylvania arrived before Gettysburg by way of the Emmitsburg road a short time after sunset on 1 July.

approach.phrase: up the pike leading to Gettysburg
approach.identification: the pike from Emmitsburg to Gettysburg, printed without its name: the gazetteer's Emmitsburg Road (the ledger references GZ-041)
approach.why: The 40th New York moved from Emmitsburg up the pike leading to Gettysburg on the morning of 2 July.

approach.phrase: the main road from Emmitsburg to Gettysburg
approach.identification: the main road from Emmitsburg to Gettysburg: the gazetteer's Emmitsburg Road (the ledger references GZ-041)
approach.why: Burling's brigade with Smith's battery joined its division about 9 a. m. on 2 July, marching by the main road from Emmitsburg to Gettysburg (Humphreys's report); the division's own cell in the PDF ledger prints another road (AP-07).

approach.phrase: moving on the Taneytown road
approach.why: Hays: on 2 July the division, moving on the Taneytown road, arrived within about a mile of the town.

approach.phrase: moving on the Baltimore pike toward Gettysburg
approach.why: On the morning of 1 July the Twelfth Corps left Littlestown moving on the Baltimore pike toward Gettysburg (Williams's report).

approach.phrase: turnpike leading from Baltimore to that place
approach.identification: the turnpike from Baltimore to Gettysburg: the Baltimore Pike (the ledger references GZ-039)
approach.why: Geary: at Two Taverns he received orders to forward the command toward Gettysburg on the turnpike leading from Baltimore, and advanced at about 3 p. m. on 1 July.

approach.phrase: marched by the Baltimore turnpike
approach.why: Kane's brigade marched by the Baltimore turnpike to Two Taverns on 1 July.

approach.phrase: moving along the Baltimore pike
approach.why: The Twelfth Corps artillery brigade moved along the Baltimore pike to a point 5 miles southeast of Gettysburg on 1 July.

approach.phrase: by the Hanover road to Gettysburg
approach.why: Colgrove's brigade went by a cross-road to the Hanover road and by the Hanover road to Gettysburg (the leg that enters the field; the corps road is the Baltimore pike).

approach.phrase: encamped on the road from Chambersburg to Gettysburg
approach.identification: the road from Chambersburg to Gettysburg, near Fayetteville and on to Cashtown: the Chambersburg Pike (the gazetteer's name); the divisions and brigades of the same corps print the same road (AP-14 to AP-18) and no formation of the corps prints another gazetteer road (Pegram's battalion calls the road to Cashtown the Baltimore pike; the ledger takes that for the printed name of the same road, and its claim PD-3c-res-art-pegram-02 is not used)
approach.why: Lt. Gen. Hill's report: on 29 June the Third Corps (Anderson, Heth, Pender and five battalions of artillery) was encamped on the road from Chambersburg to Gettysburg near Fayetteville and Hill was directed to move on this road; Heth went to Cashtown on the 29th, Pender on the 30th, Anderson on 1 July. The claim is dated 29 June and prints no clock: an approach needs the road, and the time at the field is the unit's gate (Q04). The first review left it out as 'a march before the battle'; DEC-012 reverses that for a corps-level road of the line of march that the units under it print as well.

approach.phrase: took up the line of march along the turnpike in the direction of Gettysburg
approach.identification: the turnpike through Cashtown Gap toward Gettysburg (the only road Wright prints is 'the turnpike'): the Chambersburg Pike, the gazetteer's name (the ledger prints Chambersburg-Gettysburg turnpike through Cashtown Gap and references GZ-075 Cashtown); the phrase stands about 900 characters after the claim's quote in the same report
approach.why: Wright's brigade followed Mahone's through Cashtown Gap on the morning of 1 July, was halted in the road about 10 a. m., bivouacked by the turnpike near Cashtown and about 1 p. m. took up the line of march along the turnpike in the direction of Gettysburg (Wright's report, printed p. 622). The first review left the claim out as a position beside the turnpike; the same report prints the march.

approach.phrase: the road between Taneytown and Gettysburg
approach.identification: printed as the road between Taneytown and Gettysburg: the road named by its two ends, the gazetteer’s Taneytown Road (the ledger references GZ-042, “by inference” from those words); the two ends are the words of the claim, the name is the gazetteer’s
approach.why: Dispatch of Meade’s chief of staff to the Sixth Corps, 1 July, no hour printed (OR27-3-D0967, printed p. 462): “the Second Corps is on the road between Taneytown and Gettysburg”. A position statement that puts the corps on its road to the field before it came on (it reached the field early on 2 July). The other document of the same day (the circular, POS-B-us-2c-19: the corps “now at Taneytown”) differs in place, not in road, and is listed on the card as a conflict. The statement sits inside a sentence about a possible fight (the ledger’s fidelity note); the corps’ position on the road is stated as a fact.

approach.phrase: on the Taneytown road, near the cross-road leading to Two Taverns
approach.identification: printed as the Taneytown road (the gazetteer’s name; the ledger references GZ-042): the road from Taneytown to Gettysburg, with its cross-road to Two Taverns
approach.why: Tyler’s report (OR27-1-R315, printed p. 872): the Artillery Reserve encamped on the night of 1 July on the Taneytown road near the cross-road leading to Two Taverns, i.e. on its road to the field before its batteries were posted along the Baltimore turnpike and near the Emmitsburg road on 2 July. The earlier camp at Taneytown “on the Emmitsburg turnpike” (POS-C-0324, 30 June) is the Taneytown to Emmitsburg road, a road of another place, and is not used. Read for the whole Reserve (inherited at tier plausible-procedural by its brigades and batteries; a nearer printed road overrides).

approach.phrase: 3 miles from Gettysburg, on the Hanover road
approach.identification: printed as the Hanover road: the gazetteer’s Hanover Road (the ledger references GZ-043); 3 miles from Gettysburg puts the division east of the loaded ground
approach.why: Pleasonton to Gregg, 10.40 a. m. 2 July (OR27-3-D1019, printed p. 489): “I understand your position to be 3 miles from Gettysburg, on the Hanover road”. A position statement that puts the Second Cavalry Division on the road, outside the loaded ground, before it came to the field; the same dispatch tells Gregg to hold “your present position”, and a second dispatch (1.45) sends him “to the north of Gettysburg, toward the Heidlersburg road”, which is a later move and not used.

approach.phrase: the direct road from Heidlersburg to Gettysburg
approach.identification: printed as the direct road from Heidlersburg to Gettysburg (Early’s own words; the road he formed his line across): the Heidlersburg road of the road-name concordance RC-01, which is the gazetteer’s Harrisburg Road inside the loaded ground (tier inferred; no sheet prints the name Heidlersburg on a road)
approach.why: Early’s report (OR27-2-R470, printed p. 468): after passing Heidlersburg he received Ewell’s note and “continued to move on the road I was then on toward Gettysburg”, arrived in sight of the field “on the direct road from Heidlersburg” and formed across “the Heidlersburg road”. Lee (R426 p. 317, PD-2c-early-02) and Ewell (R467, p. 444) say the same of the division. The road is the same for the brigades (Hays and Hoke print it for themselves; Gordon and Smith print it as the road of their line).
approach.printed_name: the direct road from Heidlersburg to Gettysburg

approach.phrase: arrived with my brigade on the Heidlersburg road
approach.identification: printed as the Heidlersburg road: RC-01, the gazetteer’s Harrisburg Road inside the loaded ground (tier inferred)
approach.why: Hays’s report (OR27-2-R472, printed p. 479): “arrived with my brigade on the Heidlersburg road, within a mile and a half of Gettysburg”, after a march of 13 or 14 miles from York; the brigade marched in the rear of the division column.

approach.phrase: Heidlersburg road
approach.identification: printed as the Heidlersburg road (the OCR of the quote reads Heidler.sLurg road; the ledger’s road field gives the name): RC-01, the gazetteer’s Harrisburg Road inside the loaded ground (tier inferred)
approach.why: Hoke’s report (OR27-2-R473, printed p. 484): “On July 1, we advanced upon Gettysburg, along the Heidlersburg road” and formed on the left of it 1 1/2 miles from the town.

approach.phrase: the Middletown road
approach.identification: printed as the Middletown road: the road-name concordance RC-02, which is the gazetteer’s Carlisle Road inside the loaded ground (Warren: CARLISLE ROAD and NEWVILLE ROAD; Bachelder: NEWVILLE ROAD) (tier inferred; no sheet prints the name Middletown road)
approach.why: Lee’s report (OR27-2-R426, printed p. 317): about 2.30 p. m. the advance of Ewell’s corps, Rodes’ division with Carter’s battalion, “arrived by the Middletown road”. Ewell (R467 p. 444) and Rodes (R506 pp. 552-553) print the same road for the division; Rodes puts Doles on the plain between that road and the foot of the ridge, and names the Mummasburg road, which crosses the ridge, as another road. The brigades inherit it; Daniel’s “by way of Heidlersburg” names the town of the leg before Middletown.

approach.phrase: the Middletown road
approach.identification: printed as the Middletown road: RC-02, the gazetteer’s Carlisle Road inside the loaded ground (tier inferred)
approach.why: Lee’s report (OR27-2-R426, printed p. 317) names Carter’s battalion with Rodes’ division on the Middletown road.

approach.phrase: a point on the Gettysburg road, some 2 miles from that place
approach.identification: printed as the Gettysburg road, from Fayetteville: RC-03, the Chambersburg Pike, for this passage only (tier inferred); not a name of a road elsewhere
approach.why: Kershaw’s itinerary (OR27-2-R432, printed p. 366): he marched to Fayetteville on 30 June; on 1 July “Anderson’s and Johnson’s divisions and General Ewell’s wagon train occupied the road until 4 p. m.”, when the brigade marched “to a point on the Gettysburg road, some 2 miles from that place”. Hill (R534 p. 606) puts Fayetteville on the road from Chambersburg to Gettysburg and Wright prints Anderson’s division on the turnpike (AP-32).

approach.phrase: Emmitsburg Pike
approach.identification: printed as the Emmitsburg Pike (the ledger's road field; the quote is cut after "by the Emmitsburg"): the gazetteer's Emmitsburg Road (the ledger references GZ-041); the 154th New York sketch is the commission's unsigned historian's, claim tier inferred. The other claim of the division (POS-E-US-11C-2D-001: "the circuitous route by Horner's Mills", the compiler's summary) names a route the gazetteer cannot place (RC-07) and is listed on the card as a conflicting claim; neither is resolved
approach.why: Steinwehr's division was the last of the Eleventh Corps to reach Cemetery Hill, by the Emmitsburg Pike (154th NY sketch, NY3 p. 1053-1055; one of two volumes that print the division on that pike; the 73rd PA address, PA1B p. 423, prints the junction of the Emmitsburg and Taneytown roads).

approach.phrase: on the Emmitsburg Road
approach.identification: printed as on the Emmitsburg Road, three or four miles from the smoke and exploding shell: the road is printed by name; at noon on 1 July the battery was on it, outside the loaded ground, riding toward the fight. The claim POS-E-US-11C-ART-1NYI-001 prints the same road for the morning march from the camp at Emmitsburg
approach.why: Wiedrich's battery (1st NY Light Artillery, the unsigned narrative that follows the Battery I address, NY3 p. 1246): in the morning of 1 July it left its camp at Emmitsburg by the Emmitsburg Road, and at about noon went at the gallop toward the smoke and shell three or four miles off.

Battery G, 4th US reached the town at 11 a. m. on 1 July.
Buford's dispatch: he entered Gettysburg at 11 a. m. on 30 June.
Gamble's brigade was in camp at the seminary building about 8 o'clock on the morning of 1 July.
15th New York Battery in a peach orchard at 4.30 p. m. on 2 July.
Steinwehr's division on Cemetery Hill under fire from about 4 p. m. on 2 July.

documented_absent.summary: The regiment was detailed on the night of 30 June at Taneytown to guard the supply train (Merchant's address; Lt. Col. Opp's report, OR27-1-R168 p. 557), started on 1 July with the train, which was moving with the column from Taneytown on the road to Emmitsburg, and then marched with it to Westminster, where it arrived at 7 a. m. on 2 July and picketed the roads near the wagon parks until it marched on 6 July (Opp). The Official Records' order-of-battle table marks it "guarding corps trains, and not engaged in the battle" (OR27-1-R009). Carr's letter (claim tier inferred) puts it with the train until relieved on 6 July. No claim puts the regiment on the field.
